hints: Look first at what is missing from the spectrum as well as what is present, especially around 1700 cm-1 where carbonyl groups absorb.
Notice the very broad, strong dip centred near 3300 cm-1, which is characteristic of hydrogen bonded O-H in an alcohol.
Check each given structure for any C=O group, ketone, aldehyde or carboxylic acid, and keep only the structure with O-H but no C=O.
walkthrough:
**Read the O-H region**

Look at 3200 to 3600 cm-1. There is a very broad, deep absorption with low transmittance. That is classic for an O-H group with hydrogen bonding, as in an alcohol.

Key range:
$$3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1} : \text{broad O-H (alcohol)}$$

**Check the carbonyl region**

Now look at 1680 to 1750 cm-1. There is no strong sharp dip there. The spectrum is flat and high near 1700 cm-1. That tells you there is no $\text{C=O}$ group present.

Key rule:
$$1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} : \text{sharp C=O stretch if ketone, aldehyde, acid or ester present}$$

**Match to the structures**

Structure A has a ketone $\text{C=O}$, B has an aldehyde $\text{CHO}$, and D has a carboxylic acid $\text{COOH}$. All three would show a strong C=O peak, and D would also show an even broader O-H from 2500 to 3300 cm-1. Only $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$ has only alcohol O-H groups and C-O and C-H bonds, with no C=O, which fits the spectrum perfectly.

options.A: Incorrect. HOCH2COCH2OH contains a ketone C=O plus two alcohol OH groups. It would show both a broad O-H near 3300 cm-1 and a sharp strong C=O near 1715 cm-1, but the spectrum has no C=O peak.
options.B: Incorrect. HOCH2CH(OH)CHO contains an aldehyde CHO plus alcohol OH groups. It would show a sharp C=O near 1720 cm-1 and also aldehydic C-H near 2720 and 2820 cm-1. The spectrum lacks this C=O absorption.
options.C: Correct. HOCH2CH(OH)CH2OH is propane-1,2,3-triol with three alcohol OH groups and no C=O. This matches the broad O-H absorption near 3400 cm-1, the C-H absorptions near 2900 cm-1, and the absence of any carbonyl peak near 1700 cm-1.
options.D: Incorrect. HOCH2CH2COOH is a carboxylic acid. It would show a C=O near 1710 cm-1 and a very broad O-H stretching from about 2500 to 3300 cm-1 that overlaps the C-H region. The spectrum does not show this acid pattern or a C=O peak.
